title: Beacon's Solidarity Sleepout
location: First United Methodist Church, 219 E 4th St, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Beacon's Solidarity Sleepout — Sleep out so others don't have to!

Join us on June 5th at 5pm until June 6th at 8am on the greenspace at First United Methodist Church in Bloomington. Participants will choose to sleep outside for one night to stand in solidarity with those who don't have that choice.

By asking their friends and family to sponsor them, participants will raise essential funds for Beacon's emergency shelter — the largest year-round emergency shelter for women in our area.

Let's acknowledge the realities of homelessness and inspire empathy and action as we come together to build a community where everyone has a safe place to sleep and the support they need on their path home.

To sign up or view more information, visit: sleepout.info

title: Lemonade Day 2026
description:
Lemonade Day is a free, fun, experiential learning program that teaches youth how to start, own and operate their own business – a lemonade stand.
The foremost objective of Lemonade Day is to empower youth to take ownership of their lives and become productive members of society – the business leaders, social advocates, volunteers, and forward thinking citizens of tomorrow.
Each child that registers receives access to Lemonopolis, our FREE and FUN online curriculum that teaches them Lemonade Day lessons like creating budgets, setting profit-making goals, serving customers, repaying investors, and giving back to the community. Along the way, they acquire skills in goal-setting, problem solving, and gain self-esteem critical for future success. They also receive additional digital content from local sponsors and experts on topics like Building a Lemonade Stand, Recipe Exploration, Marketing, and more!

Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: Common Threads
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART - Room Number: Roehm Family Art-making Event
description: Looking for a welcoming space to crochet, knit, embroider, quilt, and explore other fiber arts? Interested in sharing your experiences and connecting with others while learning new skills? Or even just want a place to vent while you work on your scarf you've been crocheting for 2 years? Look no further; join us for Common Threads!  Common Threads is a free program open to the public and offers a welcoming environment to share, unwind, and learn! You can bring your own fiber art to work on while working alongside others who enjoy working in fiber and textiles. Or you can try learning something new; we welcome all skill levels! Either way, you're sure to have a good time.  This group meets on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month from 3–4:30 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures. The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour
location: Lilly Library - Room Number: Slocum Room
description: Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour.  Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!

title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library
location: Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.) - Room Number: North Gallery
description: You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible, John James Audubon's Birds of America, and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections. Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road gate. The gate is locked but we have a key. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: Discardia Mending Day
location: Monroe County Public Library - Downtown, 303 E Kirkwood Ave, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Mending Day is the second Saturday of each month, noon till 4PM. Join our sewing circle as we teach, learn, help others, mend and create art.
Please be kind and pre-launder your projects.

Bring your sewing, interest in sewing, interest to learn, and willingness to teach, or just bring pre-washed fabric items in need of mending or alteration! We fix and alter garments and other fabric items for free, as a service to the greater community, for fun! Let’s keep things useful and out of landfill together!Calling all Artists, Fashion Designers, Creatives, and Community Members of All Ages Interested in Sustainable Practices.

Discardia, a program of the Center for Sustainable Living, creates an environment for local designers to brainstorm to make upcycled clothing and to teach people in the community how to upcycle their own items. Get involved with Discardia as a Mending Day Sewing Advisor: https://www.bloomingtonvolunteernetwork.org/need/detail/?need_id=355829
Discardia members and volunteer Sewing Advisors assist attendees in mending clothing, giving them an opportunity to learn how to sew or work on any other project involving clothing. Sewing machines and basic supplies are provided to participants, for free, and all ages are welcome!
Volunteer Sewing Advisors offer help to participants with altering or repairing the garments that they have brought in. Use your skills to assist participants with creative solutions, but not to make all the decisions for them.
Help is also appreciated in setting up and tearing down before and after the event (30 minutes each).
This is a great way to empower as well as collaborate with a group of creative problem solvers and learn to use the various tools and tricks of the trade to make it easier to make adjustments to our own clothes so that they fit well and are comfortable and we feel good wearing them.
All skill levels are welcome and training is provided. It's a lot of fun and makes you feel empowered and confident. Contact Stephen Hale, Discardia Project Manager if interested at 812-334-0922.

title: Another Revolution
location: Constellation Playhouse,107 West 9th Street, Bloomington, IN 47404, USA
description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Another Revolution,” on stage June 4-21 at the Constellation Playhouse.

Some revolutions happen in the streets. Others in the lab.

Kat and Henry, two graduate students from opposing scientific disciplines, are forced to share a lab at Columbia University in 1968. Amidst interpersonal differences, a campus devolving into political chaos, and the uncertainty and turmoil of the outside world, they each discover what it’s like to be thrown into someone else’s orbit. By Jacqueline Bircher, playwright of Constellation’s hit production of Webster’s B!+@#. Recommended for ages 13+.

title: Tattoo Design Workshop
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART - Room Number: Roehm Family Art-making Studio
description: Have you always wanted to design your own tattoos, but never known where to find inspiration? Start at the museum!  This monthly workshop provides instructions for examining art to find personal meaning inside it, and how to use that meaning to design tattoos based on your own life! Supplies will be provided to design tattoos. title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us. title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: Growlers Off Road Adventure Ride
description:
Bring Lights! Bring Lights! Bring Lights!
These rides feature gravel roads, single and double track trails, and just enough pavement to string the aforementioned together into fun, woodsy adventure loops. Rides begin at 6PM through the Fall and Winter months as weather allows and typically last about two hours. Lights are mandatory as we enter the Fall and Winter seasons.
Routes are suitable for mountain bike or gravel bike, with some more turned to one or the other. Rides begin at different locations, primarily associated with Yellowwood State Forest, Brown County State Park, and the Hoosier National Forest in Monroe, Lawrence, and Brown Counties. Specific routes may be dictated by weather conditions, but starting locations, route maps, and gps file links will be posted here in advance.
Expect a lot of trees and few cars
Non-members should sign up for a free trial membership, good for up to three rides, and which includes electronically signing a liability waiver, prior to participation.

location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour
location: Lilly Library - Room Number: Slocum Room
description: Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour.  Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!

title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library
location: Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.) - Room Number: North Gallery
description: You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible, John James Audubon's Birds of America, and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections. Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.

Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Growlers Off Road Adventure Ride
description:
Bring Lights! Bring Lights! Bring Lights!
These rides feature gravel roads, single and double track trails, and just enough pavement to string the aforementioned together into fun, woodsy adventure loops. Rides begin at 6PM through the Fall and Winter months as weather allows and typically last about two hours. Lights are mandatory as we enter the Fall and Winter seasons.
Routes are suitable for mountain bike or gravel bike, with some more turned to one or the other. Rides begin at different locations, primarily associated with Yellowwood State Forest, Brown County State Park, and the Hoosier National Forest in Monroe, Lawrence, and Brown Counties. Specific routes may be dictated by weather conditions, but starting locations, route maps, and gps file links will be posted here in advance.
Expect a lot of trees and few cars
Non-members should sign up for a free trial membership, good for up to three rides, and which includes electronically signing a liability waiver, prior to participation.

Each comedian is asked to do no more than five minutes of completely original material. While we do not care about foul language in your set, we do not allow racist, homophobic, transphobic or rape/female bashing jokes. If you have to ask if it's racist, homophobic, transphobic or a rape joke, it probably is.

Comedians that wish to participate are asked to e-mail comedyattic@gmail.com mailto:comedyattic@gmail.com . Newcomers and any participants who are not paid professionals will be required to bring audience members to see them. This is non-negotiable. So if you plan on signing up, be sure to invite as many friends as you can. Good luck!

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: Growlers Off Road Adventure Ride
description:
Bring Lights! Bring Lights! Bring Lights!
These rides feature gravel roads, single and double track trails, and just enough pavement to string the aforementioned together into fun, woodsy adventure loops. Rides begin at 6PM through the Fall and Winter months as weather allows and typically last about two hours. Lights are mandatory as we enter the Fall and Winter seasons.
Routes are suitable for mountain bike or gravel bike, with some more turned to one or the other. Rides begin at different locations, primarily associated with Yellowwood State Forest, Brown County State Park, and the Hoosier National Forest in Monroe, Lawrence, and Brown Counties. Specific routes may be dictated by weather conditions, but starting locations, route maps, and gps file links will be posted here in advance.
Expect a lot of trees and few cars

title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour
location: Lilly Library - Room Number: Slocum Room
description: Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour.  Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!

title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library

This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: Growlers Off Road Adventure Ride
description:
Bring Lights! Bring Lights! Bring Lights!
These rides feature gravel roads, single and double track trails, and just enough pavement to string the aforementioned together into fun, woodsy adventure loops. Expect a lot of trees and few cars

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us. To schedule a tour for groups of students in grades 2-12, see Field Trip Tours: Revolution & Reflection (https://artmuseum.indiana.edu/visit/museum-tours/tour-types.html).

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: Zach Rushing “Redneck Logic” Comedy Tour
location: Buskirk-Chumley Theater,114 East Kirkwood Avenue, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
I’m just a Mississippi boy with a loud mouth and a big heart. I grew up believing in hard work, good friends, and telling it like it is, and I never really grew out of that. Most people know me from my comedy, where I’ve built a career on being unapologetically myself. Whether I’m on stage for the Not-So-Rich-And-Famous Tour, raising hell on social media, or telling stories that hit a little too close to home, I try to keep it real and keep people laughing.

But I’m more than just a comic. I run Triple B Outdoors, where I get to share my love for hunting, fishing, and the outdoors with folks who live for the same things I do. I’m engaged to the love of my life, and when I’m not on the road, you’ll find me in the woods, on the water, or working to grow my businesses.

At the end of the day, I’m not trying to be famous, I’m just trying to be honest, entertain people, and maybe inspire a few along the way. If you stick around, you’ll get jokes, a little wisdom, and probably a few stories you wouldn’t want your grandma to hear.

This is an 18+ event.

title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour
location: Lilly Library - Room Number: Slocum Room
description: Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour.  Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!

title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library
location: Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.) - Room Number: North Gallery
description: You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible, John James Audubon's Birds of America, and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections. Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.

title: 2nd Weekend Work Day Trail Building
description:
Knobstone Hiking Trail Association of Indiana Meetup
Would you to spend a day in some beautiful woods with a delightful group of people building a connecting section of Indiana’s premier long distance hiking trail? Come join us as we continue work on the Tecumseh Trail extension portion of the KHT in MMSF. We will be building the new trail including clipping green briar.
Please bring a lunch and water. We will have large hand tools, but please bring any small tools you have such as clippers or a pruning saw. And a backpack is handy to carry everything in. Instructions will be provided for those who need them. We finish about 3:30.
Meet at the Hatfield Ridge Road gate. The gate is locked but we have a key. Go to the big sign on Rosenbaum/Catholic Cemetry Rd.
Join us on our website at http://www.knobstonehikingtrail.org/, on Facebook at [www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484](http://www.facebook.com/groups/2255586117953484), and Substack [https://khta.substack.com/](https://khta.substack.com/)

title: Discardia Mending Day
location: Monroe County Public Library - Downtown, 303 E Kirkwood Ave, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA
description:
Mending Day is the second Saturday of each month, noon till 4PM. Join our sewing circle as we teach, learn, help others, mend and create art.
Please be kind and pre-launder your projects.

Bring your sewing, interest in sewing, interest to learn, and willingness to teach, or just bring pre-washed fabric items in need of mending or alteration! We fix and alter garments and other fabric items for free, as a service to the greater community, for fun! Let’s keep things useful and out of landfill together!Calling all Artists, Fashion Designers, Creatives, and Community Members of All Ages Interested in Sustainable Practices.

Discardia, a program of the Center for Sustainable Living, creates an environment for local designers to brainstorm to make upcycled clothing and to teach people in the community how to upcycle their own items. Get involved with Discardia as a Mending Day Sewing Advisor: https://www.bloomingtonvolunteernetwork.org/need/detail/?need_id=355829
Discardia members and volunteer Sewing Advisors assist attendees in mending clothing, giving them an opportunity to learn how to sew or work on any other project involving clothing. Sewing machines and basic supplies are provided to participants, for free, and all ages are welcome!
Volunteer Sewing Advisors offer help to participants with altering or repairing the garments that they have brought in. Use your skills to assist participants with creative solutions, but not to make all the decisions for them.
Help is also appreciated in setting up and tearing down before and after the event (30 minutes each).
This is a great way to empower as well as collaborate with a group of creative problem solvers and learn to use the various tools and tricks of the trade to make it easier to make adjustments to our own clothes so that they fit well and are comfortable and we feel good wearing them.
All skill levels are welcome and training is provided. It's a lot of fun and makes you feel empowered and confident. Contact Stephen Hale, Discardia Project Manager if interested at 812-334-0922.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Revolution & Reflection: Campus Experiences in Art, History, and Ideas
description: Look for your guide, President George Washington, as you drop in to visit these three revolutionary destinations:The Lilly Library presents The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence).The Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art showcases George Washington's portrait by Gilbert Stuart.  IU Auditorium is the caretaker of Thomas Hart Benton's iconic murals (https://www.iuauditorium.com/about-us/benton-murals-organ-and-dailey-art-collection), titled The Social History of Indiana.Spend an afternoon with us. Or a whole day. This self-guided offering is designed to allow you to create your own educational experience. Visit all locations in one trip or come back to campus multiple times. Each Fine Arts Plaza destination has different operating hours; please consult them carefully when planning your trip. All locations are open Tuesday–Friday between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m.  Check our online event calendar at go.iu.edu/america-250 (https://go.iu.edu/america-250) for special events and additional campus celebrations of America's 250th.  To schedule a tour for groups of students in grades 2-12, see Field Trip Tours: Revolution & Reflection (https://artmuseum.indiana.edu/visit/museum-tours/tour-types.html).

title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment
description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?

title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection
description: When Kripke died in 2020, she left behind a remarkable collection of over 20,000 dictionaries, as well as a rich manuscript archive about dictionaries, her life, and her collecting. In 2021, the Lilly Library acquired the collection, keeping it intact and available for all to study. The spring 2026 exhibition The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection shares some of the collection publicly for the first time, curated by IU Provost Professor of English Michael Adams (https://english.indiana.edu/about/faculty/adams-michael.html) and Lilly Library Executive Associate Director Erika Dowell.  Madeline Kripke believed that dictionaries are an especially useful lens for observing culture. She focused on slang and other marginalized language, and she charted the roles of dictionaries in everyday life. She collected, not merely to possess, but to share what she saw with scholars and the public, and The Whole World in a Book realizes her ambition to do so.  This exhibition is on display until July 24, 2026. For the Lilly Library's daily hours, please visit the website (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library).

title: Common Threads
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART - Room Number: Roehm Family Art-making Event
description: Looking for a welcoming space to crochet, knit, embroider, quilt, and explore other fiber arts? Interested in sharing your experiences and connecting with others while learning new skills? Or even just want a place to vent while you work on your scarf you've been crocheting for 2 years? Look no further; join us for Common Threads!  Common Threads is a free program open to the public and offers a welcoming environment to share, unwind, and learn! You can bring your own fiber art to work on while working alongside others who enjoy working in fiber and textiles. Or you can try learning something new; we welcome all skill levels! Either way, you're sure to have a good time.  This group meets on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month from 3–4:30 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures. The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.

title: Growlers Off Road Adventure Ride
description:
Bring Lights! Bring Lights! Bring Lights!
These rides feature gravel roads, single and double track trails, and just enough pavement to string the aforementioned together into fun, woodsy adventure loops. Rides begin at 6PM through the Fall and Winter months as weather allows and typically last about two hours. Lights are mandatory as we enter the Fall and Winter seasons.
Routes are suitable for mountain bike or gravel bike, with some more turned to one or the other. Rides begin at different locations, primarily associated with Yellowwood State Forest, Brown County State Park, and the Hoosier National Forest in Monroe, Lawrence, and Brown Counties. Specific routes may be dictated by weather conditions, but starting locations, route maps, and gps file links will be posted here in advance.
Expect a lot of trees and few cars
Non-members should sign up for a free trial membership, good for up to three rides, and which includes electronically signing a liability waiver, prior to participation.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour
location: Lilly Library - Room Number: Slocum Room
description: Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour.  Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!

title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library
location: Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.) - Room Number: North Gallery
description: You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible, John James Audubon's Birds of America, and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections. Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.

The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. title: The Whole World in a Book: Celebrating Madeline Kripke's Dictionary Collection

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Tattoo Design Workshop
location: SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART - Room Number: Roehm Family Art-making Studio
description: Have you always wanted to design your own tattoos, but never known where to find inspiration? Start at the museum!  This monthly workshop provides instructions for examining art to find personal meaning inside it, and how to use that meaning to design tattoos based on your own life! Supplies will be provided to design tattoos. Occasional guests from the local tattooing community may be featured to answer questions about tattoo design, tattoo processes, or the fascinating history of tattoos.  This group meets on the 2nd Tuesday of every month, excluding holidays and museum closures. The group will meet in the Roehm Family Art-making Studio, located inside the Simpson Center for Education on the 2nd floor of the Eskenazi Museum of Art.

title: Growlers Off Road Adventure Ride
description:
Bring Lights! Bring Lights! Bring Lights!
These rides feature gravel roads, single and double track trails, and just enough pavement to string the aforementioned together into fun, woodsy adventure loops. Rides begin at 6PM through the Fall and Winter months as weather allows and typically last about two hours. Lights are mandatory as we enter the Fall and Winter seasons.
Routes are suitable for mountain bike or gravel bike, with some more turned to one or the other. Rides begin at different locations, primarily associated with Yellowwood State Forest, Brown County State Park, and the Hoosier National Forest in Monroe, Lawrence, and Brown Counties. Specific routes may be dictated by weather conditions, but starting locations, route maps, and gps file links will be posted here in advance.
Expect a lot of trees and few cars
Non-members should sign up for a free trial membership, good for up to three rides, and which includes electronically signing a liability waiver, prior to participation.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour
location: Lilly Library - Room Number: Slocum Room
description: Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour.  Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!

title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library
location: Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.) - Room Number: North Gallery
description: You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible, John James Audubon's Birds of America, and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections. Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.

title: 15th Annual Indiana State Fingerstyle Guitar Festival
location: Brown County Playhouse, 70 S. Van Buren St, Nashville, IN, 47448, United States
description:
BUY TICKETS

The 15th Annual Indiana State Fingerstyle Guitar Festival features a morning guitar competition and an evening concert! Tickets are available separately for each, or an all-day pass is available.
Fingerstyle Guitar Competition:
11:00 AM – 2:00PM
Acoustic guitarists from around the world take the stage for the 15th annual Fingerstyle Guitar Competition. The competition features two rounds of performance, showcasing a wide range of styles, techniques, and original music. At the conclusion of the competition, the top three players will be awarded grand-prize guitars and earn the honor of performing in the Evening Concert.
Evening Concert:
7:30 PM
The Evening Concert features fingerstyle guitar legend Muriel Anderson, with special guests Tim Thompson and Jack Wilson. The concert will open with performances by the top three competition winners, giving audiences the chance to hear tomorrow’s guitar greats alongside established masters.
Muriel Anderson is internationally celebrated for her mastery of the 20-string harp-guitar, her versatility across musical genres, and her warm, engaging stage presence. She was the first woman to win the National Fingerstyle Guitar Championship, and Guitar Player Magazine has named her one of the Top 50 Guitarists of All Time. Recently recognized among the Top Ten Female Guitarists, Muriel’s lasting legacy lies in her uplifting compositions and deeply expressive performances.
She has recorded with country legend Chet Atkins, performed with Les Paul and countless other greats in “Muriel Anderson’s All Star Guitar Night®” over the past 30+ years. Muriel’s CD Nightlight Daylight placed first in its category in 11 national awards, followed by Acoustic Chef, an international CD with cookbook. Muriel’s release Sailing Dreams exhibits new levels of creativity–she has even created a board game to accompany the music.
Jack Wilson is a Chicagoland-based guitarist and 2013 Indiana Guitar Fest Champion. He won 1st place at the 2016 International Fingerstyle Guitar Competition at the Walnut Valley Festival after placing second in 2015. Appearing multiple times as a featured performer on our stage, Jack is a chameleon of a player, being able to shift comfortably from acoustic to electric, pick or fingerstyle in a wide range of styles, and immediately gets your attention by producing a cowbell sound from the guitar from his version of “Low Rider”.
Tim Thompson is a Nashville-based fingerstyle guitarist and a two-time International Fingerstyle Guitar Champion. Long associated with our guitar festival, Tim’s career includes extensive session work and collaborations across genres, appearing with artists like Tommy Emmanuel, Crystal Gayle, and Hwy 101. He has recorded eleven CDs and two DVDs. He has been featured in the Taylor Guitar’s Wood and Steel, Just Jazz Guitar and Fingerstyle Guitar which said, “Tim Thompson is a Nashville based finger-stylist that burns!”
Ticket Information
Front & Center Tickets are limited to the first four rows in the center section of the theater and offer the closest possible view of the stage.

title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature
location: LILLY LIBRARY - Room Number: Ball Room
description: "Myths are the world’s dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past and reunite us with the beliefs and stories of our ancestors.Most of these materials originate from the collection of prolific miniature book collector, Ruth Elizabeth Adomeit (1910-1996). Notable book artists highlighted inMicro-Mythologies include Maryline Poole Adams, Carol Cunningham, Barbara J. Raheb, Dianne Weiss, and Gabrielle Fox.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is curated by Curatorial Assistant Jake Gentry, with counsel from Sarah McElroy Mitchell, Curator of Religious Collections. In addition, exhibition design was done by Jenny Mack and graphic design by David Orr. This exhibition is on display in the Lilly Library Ball Room through December 2026.

description: Looking for a welcoming space to crochet, knit, embroider, quilt, and explore other fiber arts? Interested in sharing your experiences and connecting with others while learning new skills? Or even just want a place to vent while you work on your scarf you've been crocheting for 2 years? Look no further; join us for Common Threads!  Common Threads is a free program open to the public and offers a welcoming environment to share, unwind, and learn! You can bring your own fiber art to work on while working alongside others who enjoy working in fiber and textiles. Or you can try learning something new; we welcome all skill levels! Either way, you're sure to have a good time.  This group meets on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday of each month from 3–4:30 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures. description:
Every Wednesday at 8PM is Comedy Attic Open Mic Night. Bloomington has one of the best local comedy scenes in the country, and it all starts with our open mic night!

Each comedian is asked to do no more than five minutes of completely original material. While we do not care about foul language in your set, we do not allow racist, homophobic, transphobic or rape/female bashing jokes. If you have to ask if it's racist, homophobic, transphobic or a rape joke, it probably is.
